ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BAC=60^\circ$, $\angle BCE=40^\circ$, $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, $CE \perp AB$ at point E, then what is the degree measure of $\angle ADC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $CE\perp AB$,
\[\therefore \angle BEC=90^\circ,\]
Since \(\angle BCE=40^\circ\),
\[\therefore \angle B=50^\circ,\]
Since \(\angle BAC=60^\circ\) and $AD$ bisects \(\angle BAC\),
\[\therefore \angle BAD=\frac{1}{2}\angle BAC=30^\circ,\]
\[\therefore \angle ADC=\angle B+\angle BAD\]
\[=50^\circ+30^\circ\]
\[=\boxed{80^\circ}.\]

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, A is the upper vertex of triangle ABC, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, B, D, C are on the same straight-line base, and D is located on BC. E is located on side AB, segment AD connects from A to D, and segment CE connects from C to E. Reasoning: From the problem statement, CE ⟂ AB, and E is on AB, so ∠BEC = 90°. In triangle BCE, it is known that ∠BCE = 40°, therefore ∠CBE = 180° - 90° - 40° = 50°. Because E is on AB, ∠CBE is triangle ABC's ∠ABC, therefore ∠ABC = 50°. Also because ∠BAC = 60°, AD bisects ∠BAC, so ∠BAD = 30°. In triangle ABD, D, B, C are collinear, and DC is the extension of DB, therefore ∠ADC is the exterior angle of triangle ABD at point D. By the exterior angle theorem, ∠ADC = ∠ABD + ∠BAD = 50° + 30° = 80°.
